item.title: Mini Crackme: sub/neg magnitude check
item.description:
Target: Windows x86-64 (calling convention: ecx = arg1). ecx holds a 32-bit signed integer. Find the value of ecx that makes check return 1.
check: mov eax, ecx sub eax, 777 ; eax = x - 777 neg eax ; eax = -(x - 777) = 777 - x cmp eax, 1000 jne fail mov eax, 1 ret fail: xor eax, eax ret
What value of ecx makes check return 1?
---
Answer: ecx = -223 (0xFFFFFF21)
neg computes the two's-complement negation of its operand -- it's equivalent to 0 - eax, so after sub eax, 777 (giving x - 777), the neg turns that into 777 - x.
The cmp/jne pair requires 777 - x == 1000, so solving backward gives x = 777 - 1000 = -223.
Passing ecx = -223 makes eax land on exactly 1000 after the sub/neg pair, so the jne falls through and check returns 1.
